source.:question/worked-solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}⁡x)=\frac{1}{xln⁡a}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{log}_{4}⁡x) \\  & =5\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{4}⁡x) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡4} \\  & =\frac{5}{xln⁡4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given the function $y=4{x}^{2}-6{log}_{3}x,$ find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$ Do not round the answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is
{{field-1}}.
source.:question/worked-solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{2}-6{log}_{3}x) \\  & =4\cdot 2x-6\cdot \frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}3} \\  & =8x-\frac{6}{x\operatorname{ln}3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(8x-\frac{6}{x\operatorname{ln}3})|}_{x=1} \\  & =8(1)-\frac{6}{1\cdot \operatorname{ln}3} \\  & =8-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
